solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Daughter invested in black and white set lacking electronic capacity

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into a venture
set means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged
lacking means going without, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its final letter
the letter dropped is the last of the colour word
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone with a black and white television set complains it cannot cope with modern electronic signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops the E of WHITE to leave WHIT; 'invested in' puts D inside, and 'set' rearranges those letters into WIDTH, after B AND. Arguably 'lacking electronic' is the E-removal, the abbreviation for electronic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies, hence the data capacity, a channel or circuit can carry.

clue.text: Extremely poor recording of player

indicators.note: a recording reproduces sound, so the word is given as it is heard

parts.note: a bassist is a player of the bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A dreadful recording of a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Basest is the superlative of base, meaning lowest in quality or most contemptible.

clue.text: Screen I monitor picked up hidden figure entering field?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards
hidden means concealed within the phrase

explanation.surface: Instructions for a screening: a monitor is lifted to spot a hidden intruder in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Screen I monitor' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward is one of the field of contenders entered for a vote or award.

clue.text: After turn west the Doctor's craft's heading off, arrives in archipelago

indicators.note: after means following, so the compass letter comes next

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, and off means removed

parts.note: the TARDIS is Doctor Who's time-travelling spacecraft
lands means arrives, as a plane does

explanation.surface: A sci-fi time machine turns west and touches down among some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Doctor' is Doctor Who, hero of the BBC science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windward Islands are a Caribbean chain within the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Penned in bold or iconoclastic style

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A writer works in a bold, rule-breaking manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, a plain style of column.

clue.text: Inched awkwardly round bolted barrier

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: bolted means ran off

explanation.surface: Someone edged clumsily around a locked barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolted' seems to mean locked, but it means ran away.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is an obstacle, something that blocks progress.

clue.text: Ad for Jan, say

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
January is an example of a month, abbreviated MO

explanation.surface: A short advertisement placed on behalf of someone called Jan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jan' looks like a person's name, but it is short for January, a month (MO).
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional piece, an advertisement in informal speech.

clue.text: Chained so uncomfortably in custody? This could have unfortunate consequences

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: being in custody means held by the police

indicators.note: uncomfortably means awkwardly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner chained painfully in a cell is warned that this will end badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an apparent prize or job that is likely to bring trouble.

clue.text: Ham and eggs — the Queen tucked in in front of court

indicators.note: in front of means coming before, so the next piece follows
tucked in means placed snugly inside the other piece

parts.note: ova are eggs, the Latin plural
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A breakfast of ham and eggs eaten by the Queen at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like breakfast meat, but it is a verb: to overplay a part.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Balls in contact with trade union about proposal

indicators.note: in contact with means touching, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Footballs bounced near a union official during a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening approach or offer made to start negotiations.

clue.text: Marines disrupted session

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meeting of marines is broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class or meeting for discussion, a teaching session.

clue.text: Quality of the simple roll and French mineral water

indicators.note: to roll is to turn over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: et is French for and
Evian is a well-known brand of French bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: A lunch order: a bread roll and a bottle of French mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' seems to be bread; it is the instruction to turn ET EVIAN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is the innocence or unworldliness characteristic of simple, guileless people.

clue.text: Power source getting current in all directions

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: the four compass points, south, north, east and west, abbreviated S, N, E, W
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A power station whose current is distributed in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinews are tendons and, figuratively, the strength or mainstay behind something, as in the sinews of war.

clue.text: Bird's soft sound interrupted by marine with angry tirade

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the next piece follows on
interrupted by means broken into by the other piece

parts.note: a coo is the soft murmuring sound of a dove
RM stands for Royal Marines
a rant is an angry, ranting speech

explanation.surface: A bird's gentle cooing is cut short by a sailor's furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a large dark diving seabird.

clue.text: Rejection of expensive bathroom by landlord

parts.note: dear means costly
john is American slang for a lavatory
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A landlord refuses a tenant's request for a pricey new bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is someone who lets out property, not a piece of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dear John letter is one ending a romance, a written rejection.

clue.text: Like certain gases, not sensible to sniff

definitions.meaning: carbon monoxide and nitrogen give off no smell
sensible here means perceptible, so this is something the nose cannot detect

explanation.surface: A warning that it is unwise to inhale some gases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensible' seems to mean wise, but here it means perceptible by the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any smell, as some gases are, it cannot be perceived by the nose.

clue.text: Lowering fish under boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so it comes after

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish being dropped down from a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowering' (to lour) means frowning darkly, not letting down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering means looking sullen or threatening, just like frowning angrily.

clue.text: Spill incurs eco-taxes? Here's a good get-out

indicators.note: to spill is to scatter, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: If a spill brings environmental taxes, the polluter wants a watertight way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbreakable justification is a perfect escape route from blame.

clue.text: Southern drink to make dotty

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Southern liquor drives one mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' looks like crazy; it means covered in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting or drawing with many small dots.

clue.text: African dictator, after time held by storm troopers, shows ability to keep going

indicators.note: held by means enclosed within the other piece

parts.note: the SA (Sturmabteilung) were the Nazi storm troopers

indicators.note: after means following, so the dictator's name comes next

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: A ruthless African dictator outlasts his captors.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the capacity to sustain prolonged effort.

clue.text: In the countryside, it may be green energy

definitions.text: In the countryside, it may be green
definitions.meaning: a rubber boot, classically green, is worn in muddy countryside
in British slang, giving something some welly means putting effort or force into it

explanation.surface: Rural life and renewable power.
explanation.walkthrough: Green rubber boots are a British countryside staple; 'green energy' looks like renewable power.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Wellington boot, and British slang for vigour or power.

clue.text: Trial grew uncontrollably on a mass scale

indicators.note: uncontrollably means wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A legal trial grew out of all proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large means magnified or on a greater, more conspicuous scale.

clue.text: With difficulty, making Earl sovereign

parts.note: a king is a sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: An earl being made a monarch only after a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out a living is scraping it together, managing to produce it only with effort.

clue.text: Reduce racket in casualty

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: A and E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department
a bat is a racket, as used in table tennis

explanation.surface: Someone tries to cut down the noise in a hospital emergency ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise; it is a bat. Casualty is the British name for a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or diminish, as a storm abates.

clue.text: Halting leader's missing point — to make an impression

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and missing means it is dropped

parts.note: halting means limping, walking unevenly
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: A faltering leader misses the point while trying to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge is to have an effect or impact on something, leaving a mark.

clue.text: Primary language, one recalled when touring Italy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: touring means going round, so these letters surround the other piece
recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Latin is a language
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A first language is remembered on a tour of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: LATIN and I go round I (Italy) to make LAITINI, which 'recalled' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or earliest, the same as primary.

clue.text: Visitors deprived of tea, you say? Imagine!

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: guests are visitors
tea sounds like the letter T when spoken

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that the visitors were given no tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to suppose or conjecture, much as one imagines something.

clue.text: To isolate grease, get liquid

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, not fixed, so these letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: to separate grease, melt it to a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart or separate from the rest.
